outlier.evidence: Ratings 7 (Reviewer_2zgs), 6 (Reviewer_t2Mz), 7 (Reviewer_skyx) and 6 (Reviewer_K4pY), confidence 3 to 4. The spread is one point. All four reviews are specific, and all four reviewers replied to the rebuttal.

checkable_claims.claim: The required depth is polynomial in the injectivity radius and exponential in the curvature.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 233-235: for bounded V-number, Theorem 3.1 gives a polynomial dependence of L on Delta and an exponential one on kappa (the term exp(C' len(M) kappa-hat)).

checkable_claims.claim: Theorem 3.2 needs width n of order L^99 and sample size N of order L^10.
checkable_claims.evidence: Theorem 3.2 (page 7): n = K' L^99 log^9(1/delta) log^18(L n0) and N >= L^10. Reviewer_K4pY makes the same L^99 point. The authors trace both rates to the dynamics theorem of Buchanan et al. (their Theorem G.1).

checkable_claims.claim: At line 122, f_* has the wrong domain and range; it should map into {-1, 1}.
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 122 reads 'f_* : {±1} -> R'. Reviewer_jk5n in B flags the same line. The authors concede.

checkable_claims.claim: At line 140, the step-size condition tau < lambda_1 should be tau*lambda_1 < 1.
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 140 reads 'with bounded step size tau < lambda_1'. Reviewer_xaXB in B flags the same. The authors concede: 'it should be tau < 1/lambda_1'.

checkable_claims.claim: Figure 2 has a significant error, as Appendix A.1 notes.
checkable_claims.evidence: The appendix is not in the PDF, but the authors concede the error. The camera-ready rebuilds Figure 2: M+ becomes a large circle that crosses the centre, not 'a fixed small circle at the center'.

checkable_claims.claim: Arora et al. (2019), 'Fine-grained analysis of optimization and generalization', is missing from related work.
checkable_claims.evidence: The submission cites only another Arora paper (Enhanced Convolutional NTK). The camera-ready adds the fine-grained analysis paper (ref. [27]).

checkable_claims.claim: The paper's 'injectivity radius' is not the Riemannian-geometry injectivity radius.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 2.2 defines Delta as the minimum angle between points more than tau_1 apart in intrinsic distance, not the radius on which the exponential map is a diffeomorphism. The authors agreed. The camera-ready says 'angle injectivity radius'.

rebuttal.evidence: Reviewer_t2Mz edited on 2021-08-20 and posted 'Thank you for the clarification. Increase my score.' Its review still ends 'the current version is not ready for publication', so the earlier rating was below 6. Reviewer_skyx (2021-08-20), Reviewer_K4pY (2021-08-21) and Reviewer_2zgs (2021-08-28) replied and kept their scores.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: t2Mz cited the answers (in-class terms in Delta and the V-number, the d > 1 extension, the Figure 2 fix, the added citation) and 'a promising direction in deep learning theory'. K4pY accepted that Theorem 3.2 covers actual gradient descent, not a fixed kernel, and the terminology fix. skyx and K4pY accepted that the L^99 and L^10 rates come from the borrowed NTK dynamics analysis. 2zgs accepted the NTK-regime answer. The rebuttal did not answer skyx's request for experiments; skyx kept 7.

ac.evidence: 'The reviewers all agreed that the paper contains interesting ideas and insightful theoretical results, and recommended acceptance. A few reviewers expressed minor concerns and suggestions.' This matches the post-rebuttal ratings 7, 6, 7, 6. The meta-review names no specific weakness.

main_reasons_for_decision: All four ratings at 6 or 7 after Reviewer_t2Mz raised its score
First end-to-end generalization guarantee for deep networks on nonlinear low-dimensional data
Depth-as-localization proof of the certificate problem seen as reusable (2zgs, t2Mz, K4pY)
Huge width, sample and depth requirements, NTK regime and 1-D scope treated as minor or future work

outlier.evidence: The 4 is the only rating below 6 across both committees. Its central claim, 'the authors didn't provide any comments and discussion on these sufficient conditions', is contradicted by lines 226-240, which discuss how the depth bound depends on Delta and kappa and why it may be pessimistic. It asks for toy examples, which Figures 2 and 3 give as numerical certificate experiments. Its valid points (a very large depth requirement, the line-122 typo) were also made by reviewers who recommended acceptance. Confidence 3, 'Math/other details were not carefully checked', no reply to the rebuttal and no edit. One valid core remains: the bounds use unspecified absolute constants, so no concrete depth can be computed for an example.

inattentive_reviews.evidence: A generic 200-word main review that opens by repeating its own summary. Its main objection (no discussion of the sufficient conditions) and its request for toy examples are both contradicted by the submission (lines 226-240; Figures 2 and 3). It never answered the authors' long reply.

checkable_claims.claim: The authors give no comments or discussion on the sufficient conditions of Theorems 3.1 and 3.2.
checkable_claims.evidence: Lines 226-240 discuss them: depth is a fitting resource; for bounded V-number the depth is polynomial in 1/Delta and exponential in kappa; the bounds may be pessimistic for easy instances. Section 2.2 explains each geometric parameter. No worked example gives a numerical L, because the constants are unspecified.

checkable_claims.claim: Simulations and toy examples are needed to support and illustrate the theorems.
checkable_claims.evidence: Figure 2 plots the certificate norm against the V-number on clover-shaped toy curves. Figure 3 shows the certificate for depths L = 10 and 100. The submission has no network-training experiment; the camera-ready adds a preliminary one (Appendix A.3).

checkable_claims.claim: Line 122 has the domain and range of f_* wrong.
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 122 reads 'f_* : {±1} -> R'. The authors concede.

checkable_claims.claim: The depth lower bound in Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 is negatively correlated with the clover number, so a small clover number makes L extremely large.
checkable_claims.evidence: Theorem 3.1 has the term (Delta*sqrt(1+kappa^2))^(-C''V(M)). Since Delta <= tau_1 = 1/(sqrt(20)*kappa-hat) and kappa-hat >= max(kappa, pi/2), the base is below 1, so the term grows with V. Lines 204-205 call V 'typically small'. The authors' reply says the same; haaa kept 6.

checkable_claims.claim: The paper does not address its limitations.
checkable_claims.evidence: Section 5, 'Closing the gap to real networks and data', says the rates 'are far from optimal' and names the open extensions (image models, CNNs).

checkable_claims.claim: At lines 139-140, tau < lambda_1 should be tau < 1/lambda_1.
checkable_claims.evidence: Line 140 reads 'tau < lambda_1'. The authors concede. Reviewer_t2Mz in A found the same.

rebuttal.evidence: No B reviewer posted in the discussion. Reviewer_haaa's 2021-09-02 edit adds 'After reading the rebuttal and other reviewers' comments, I decide to maintain my score.' Reviewer_xaXB edited on 2021-08-31 with no comment. Its text ('I am on the fence about this paper, but recommend acceptance') reads like a lower score than 8, so the 8 may be a post-rebuttal raise, but the record does not show it. Reviewer_qqCj and Reviewer_jk5n never edited.
rebuttal.what_convinced_or_not: The reply corrected haaa's misreading of the clover-number dependence, but haaa kept 6. The reply to jk5n pointed to Section 4, Appendix E.1 and Figures 2 and 3 and promised training experiments; jk5n never answered and kept 4. The reply to xaXB argued that kernel-method theory gives no quantitative guarantees for such geometries.

ac.evidence: A poster matches three of four ratings at 6 or more and the 6.5 mean. The text, though, lists only weaknesses: 'One reviewer raised concerns regarding the clarity and novelty of the presented results and missing supporting experiments' (jk5n), 'a bit difficult to decipher' (close to haaa), 'some polynomial terms are of very high orders'. 'Some critical regularity conditions are insufficiently explained' matches no review. It gives no reason to accept and does not mention the two 8s.

shared_issues: Impractical resource requirements: width L^99, N >= L^10, depth exponential in curvature (A: skyx, K4pY, t2Mz; B: jk5n, haaa, AC)
Gap between the NTK-regime analysis and practical training (A: 2zgs, K4pY; B: qqCj, xaXB)
Only one-dimensional curves; extension to d-dimensional manifolds (A: t2Mz, K4pY; B: xaXB)
No numerical experiments on network training (A: skyx; B: jk5n, haaa, AC)
Same typos: step size at line 140 (A: t2Mz; B: xaXB) and f_* at line 122 (A: skyx; B: jk5n)
verdict: Both committees recommended a poster with the same mean rating, 6.5, for the same reasons. Reviewers on both sides saw the first end-to-end generalization guarantee for a deep network on nonlinear low-dimensional data. Its core is a new proof that depth localizes the NTK, which solves the certificate problem that Buchanan et al. left open. Both sides also saw the same weaknesses: NTK regime only, one-dimensional curves only, width L^99 and N >= L^10, a depth bound exponential in curvature with unspecified constants, and no training experiments. Each majority called these future work. The committees differed only in spread. A was tight (7, 6, 7, 6); every reviewer answered the rebuttal, and Reviewer_t2Mz raised a below-threshold score to 6. B was split (8, 4, 6, 8). Reviewer_jk5n's 4 says the authors never discuss their sufficient conditions, but lines 226-240 do; it asks for toy examples that Figures 2 and 3 give, and jk5n never answered the rebuttal. Reviewer_haaa (confidence 2) read the depth bound as falling with the clover number; Theorem 3.1 makes it rise. B's AC restated the dissent but followed the majority. A spotlight was never in play: A's top score is 7, and B's two 8s come with 'on the fence' (Reviewer_xaXB) and 'relies heavily' on prior work (Reviewer_qqCj). Neither committee reacted when the authors disclosed, in both forums, that both theorems need an unstated assumption (curves in a spherical cap of radius pi/2); the camera-ready adds it.
